cases.title: Fade Out
cases.author: Ivan & Claude
cases.blurb: Hollywood, 1946. Movie star Rex Calloway is found shot in his convertible below the Hollywoodland Sign, his famous face gone. His wife identified him in under a minute. The studio wants it called an accident.
testNotes: Briefing: was it clear where to start, and which leads felt most urgent?
Pacing: on which day did your group make its first real breakthrough?
Movement: did you spend more actions travelling than asking questions?
Search cards: did any search feel like a wasted action?
Responses: were any answers confusing, or unclear about what to do next?
Solve tokens: on which day did someone first use one, and were they right?
Epilogue: did it explain everything, or leave you with "huh?" moments?
chiselNotes: The twist: on which day did the detectives suspect the dead man was not Rex? Which clue did it: Nick's alibi, the coroner's report or the usher at Grauman's (25)?
Rex: on which day was he found at the Chateau Marmont (26), and through which route: the search of Hask or Lila Moss at (38)?
Mystery card 1: did placing it over Case card A confuse anyone when they asked about card A afterwards?
Ruby: did the postcard (card I, face up) point at her too early, or did the other suspects keep her in doubt?
The weapon: on which day was the .38 found at Sunset Pier (15)? Did anyone use the "no shell casings, so a revolver" clue?
Nick's alibi ("at my tables till one"): too big a giveaway, or overlooked?
Lies: which ones did you use most? Was there a moment you wanted a lie that wasn't there? Note the suspect and card.
Wrong guesses: did anyone accuse Rex, Nick, Margo or Hask, and why?

cases.title: The Last Encore
cases.author: Ivan & Claude
cases.blurb: A trumpet player is found dead in his hotel room next to an empty bottle of sleeping pills. The coroner says sleeping pills don't do that. A short case that shows every part of the system.
testNotes: New players: is this a good first case? Which rules did you have to look up?
Length: how many days did it take, and did it feel too short?
Briefing: was it clear where to start?
chiselNotes: Dr. Pike: on which day was he found, and how: the pill bottle at the crime scene (32), Vera's lie or Moretti?
Pike's office (48): once players knew about it, was the rat poison too easy to reach?
Vera's chloroform: did it work as a red herring?
Three suspects: did you have enough lies to play with, and which suspect needs more?
Solve: was the case solved too early? Note the day.
